newsitem.title: GERMANY: EMU will cut costs for European firms - Ifo report.
newsitem.headline: EMU will cut costs for European firms - Ifo report.

text.p: The switch to a single currency will bring a significant cut in currency management costs for European companies, the German economic research institute Ifo predicted this weekend.

In a study prepared for the European Commission, Ifo calculated the total administrative costs of dealing with the EU's various currencies at 58.1 billion Ecus in 1995 -- around one percent of total gross domestic product (GDP).

Once the euro is launched, as is planned in January 1999, these costs could be cut to as little as 0.2 percent of GDP, Ifo said. The precise saving would depend on how many countries take part in the monetary union from the start.
Ifo also detailed the results of a survey of currency risk management strategies in the European Union.
"It is perhaps not surprising that most firms hedge their risk using futures contracts. Larger firms are also increasingly using options," Ifo said.
Ifo also noted that in Germany, the vast majority of large firms favoured moving production abroad to hedge against currency risk. Smaller firms tended to opt to concentrate on the home market.
